title: routing-contract-linter-and-canary-automation-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures our current working approach for: 1) the routing rule declaration (compact JSON schema we enforce), 2) the linter/contract checks that validate backward compatibility and safety, and 3) the automated canary/rollout choreography for multi-region deployments.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to all control-plane route objects (route-declarations used by the edge router and runtime policy engine).
- Must be compact enough to author in templates (Terraform/Helm/CLI) and strict enough to detect misconfigurations early.
- Safety-first: any automated rollout must include circuit-breakers at several layers (validation, metrics gates, fallback).

Quick overview (TL;DR):
- Use the "routing contract" JSON schema below as the single source of truth for route config.
- Run the routing-linter in CI and pre-commit; it enforces schema, semantics, and safety checks (no 100% traffic to unvetted model, weight sums and region coverage).
- Canary flow: dry-validate -> 1% regional canary (5–15 min) -> 10% progressive -> 50% -> full. Automated metrics check at each step: latency P50/P95, error-rate, downstream 5XXs, token-cost deltas, and quality regression signals (if available).

Routing contract (compact JSON schema, simplified):
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "routingContract",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "match", "targets", "strategy"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9-]{3,64}$"},
    "match": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "path": {"type": "string"},
        "methods": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "headers": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}}
      }
    },
    "targets": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["backend", "weight", "variant"],
        "properties": {
          "backend": {"type": "string"},
          "variant": {"type": "string"},
          "weight": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0},
          "regionAffinity": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
        }
      }
    },
    "strategy": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["type"],
      "properties": {
        "type": {"type": "string", "enum": ["weighted", "latency-optimized", "cost-optimized"]},
        "rollout": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["manual", "automated"]},
            "phases": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "pct": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 100},
                  "duration_minutes": {"type": "number", "minimum": 1},
                  "health_checks": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "annotations": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}}
  }
}

Important schema semantics (non-schema checks done by linter):
- Sum(weights) within a single region-scope must equal 100 when the route is region-scoped; if global, weights are normalized but total should be >0.
- Disallow a single unvetted variant from receiving >10% traffic in automated rollouts unless explicitly marked as "experimental" in annotations.
- If "regionAffinity" is present, verify that backend supports that region (lookup via inventory API).
- Reject configs that lack a rollback_target (see annotations convention below).

Linter rules (what CI/PR checks enforce):
- Schema validation (structure, types, required fields).
- Semantic checks: weight sums, prohibited wildcard headers, invalid HTTP verbs, suspicious regexes in path (e.g. catastrophic backtracking patterns).
- Backward-compatibility diff rules: non-breaking updates allowed: weight adjustment, adding new target with 0 weight, annotations. Breaking updates: changing match semantics (path => new path prefix semantics), removing targets, changing route id. Breaking updates must be gated behind manual approval and a migration plan.
- Safety heuristics: deny any rule that directs 100% of traffic to a backend with "status": "unhealthy" in inventory, or to targets with mismatched quantization/model-family tags.
- Enforce presence of observability hooks: metrics_exporter: "true" annotation, and at least one logging_sink in annotations.

Rollout mechanics (automated sequence):
1) Pre-checks (dry-validate): run schema + linter + quick inventory checks.
2) Staging push: route applied to staging control-plane (no production traffic). Run synthetic traffic tests that exercise typical sequences (short prompt, long prompt, streaming).
3) Canary region slice (default 1%): create a canary route object with the same id + .canary suffix, set target weights, and apply "canary-expires-at" annotation.
4) Canary monitoring window: default 10 minutes (configurable). Metrics evaluated every minute via the rollout controller. Gate rules:
   - p50 latency increased by >25% => fail
   - p95 latency increased by >40% => fail
   - Error rate (5xx or model runtime failures) increase >1% absolute OR 3x baseline => fail
   - Token cost per request increases >15% without quality improvement signals => manual review
   - Quality regression signals (from eval harness): composite score drop >0.5% => fail unless manually bypassed with risk approval
5) Progressive steps: typical automated phases: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Each phase waits for the configured duration and must pass gates.
6) Rollback: on failure, controller automatically shifts traffic back to rollback_target (annotation: rollback-target: <variant>) and creates a rollback audit entry in control-plane.

Multi-region specifics and pitfalls:
- Region-aware weight normalization: when authoring a "global" route, the controller builds per-region view based on available backends and normalizes weights so local failovers keep proportions. The linter checks that any region where the sum of available weights is <10% of global desired indicates a capacity/placement problem.
- Cross-region canaries: only allowed if backend supports synchronous replication and the inventory shows "cross-region-tested": "true". Otherwise canaries must be region-local.
- DNS TTL / cold-cache effects: when moving traffic between regions, expect a bump in latency due to cold KV cache; rollout gates must tolerate a one-off spike if within a short window (document in annotations: cache-warm-policy).

Annotations convention (lightweight opt-ins):
- "rollback-target": variant-id for safe automatic rollback.
- "canary-expires-at": ISO-8601 timestamp for auto-cleanup.
- "quality-eval-set": id of the prompt set to evaluate during canary.
- "owners": comma-separated list of oncall/team ids.
- "safety-review": url to safety signoff doc.

Example route declaration (author-friendly YAML equivalent):
---
id: products-api-prompt-route
match:
  path: /v1/generate
  methods: [POST]
targets:
  - backend: models/gpt-4-xxl
    variant: v3-quantized
    weight: 90
    regionAffinity: [us-west1, us-east1]
  - backend: models/llama-2-13b
    variant: v1
    weight: 10
strategy:
  type: weighted
  rollout:
    mode: automated
    phases:
      - pct: 1
        duration_minutes: 10
        health_checks: ["latency_p50", "error_rate", "eval_quality"]
      - pct: 10
        duration_minutes: 20
        health_checks: ["latency_p95", "error_rate"]
annotations:
  rollback-target: v3-quantized
  quality-eval-set: prompts/products-launch-2026
  owners: eng-products, oncall-sre

Common failure modes we see in practice:
- Author sets weight sums inconsistently across region-scoped manifests -> results in silent normalization that causes small regions to get no traffic. Linter must flag region manifest divergences.
- Missing rollback-target: automated controller cannot revert and requires manual intervention.
- Canaries run with synthetic load but missing real-world sampling (e.g., streaming vs non-streaming) and miss regressions. Add sampling policy to ensure representative traffic.
- Human-in-the-loop bypasses without audit cause configuration drift; require approval notes in annotations if bypassed.

Operational hooks for SREs and platform:
- rollout-controller exposes events to /control-plane/events and emits AuditIDs for each phase.
- Rapid rollback CLI: redwoodctl route rollback <route-id> --to <variant> --reason "<text>". This creates a permanent alias and attaches the audit.
- Emergency kill-switch: redwoodctl route detach <route-id> --force sets route to safe-default and notifies owners.

Developer ergonomics and CI integration:
- Pre-commit: routing-linter run (python CLI) with autofix suggestions for minor problems (e.g., missing annotations).
- PR checks: run full linter + canary-simulated dry-run (no traffic) which validates phased durations and gate config.
- Templates: provide route template snippets for common patterns (global weight, region-local, experimental).

Next steps and open questions:
- Add automated quality eval integration so rollout gates can read real-time eval signals (work with applied-ml).
- Define exact cost-signal thresholding and where to surface cost tradeoffs in console.
- Consider a "soft-fail" mode for non-critical rules in staging to reduce friction while keeping strict prod enforcement.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but pragmatic. Please comment on the recommended automated gate thresholds and whether they are conservative enough for enterprise SLAs.
- If you have runbooks or PRs that touch the rollout-controller, link them in the PR.

-- Ava
